episodes.label: Failed United Copper Stock Manipulation
episodes.summary: On October 16, 1907, New York speculators F. Augustus Heinze and Charles W. Morse failed in their attempt to corner United Copper Company stock, which was the triggering event of the 1907 Panic of 1907

episodes.label: Runs on Heinze/Morse Affiliated Banks
episodes.summary: Following the failed October 16 1907 United Copper stock manipulation by speculators Augustus Heinze and Charles Morse, depositor confidence eroded, triggering widespread runs on banks and affiliated financial institutions associated with Heinze and Morse in New York, marking the initial liquidity stress phase of the 1907 Panic.

episodes.label: NYCH Intervention to Stabilize Member Banks
episodes.summary: On October 20, 1907, the New York Clearing House (NYCH) intervened to end runs on its member banks affiliated with Heinze and Morse by issuing public solvency assurances, forcing problematic bank management to resign, and providing loan support to the troubled institutions.

episodes.label: Knickerbocker Trust Run and Aid Denial
episodes.summary: On October 21, 1907, Knickerbocker Trust faced intensifying depositor runs after its emergency aid requests to the New York Clearing House and J.P. Morgan were rejected, its president Charles Barney was dismissed, and its clearing agent National Bank of Commerce terminated its clearing service for the firm.

episodes.label: Knickerbocker Suspension and Panic Spread to Trusts
episodes.summary: On October 22, 1907, Knickerbocker Trust suspended operations after depositors withdrew approximately $8 million amid a bank run, triggering widespread depositor runs on other New York trust companies and escalating systemic liquidity stress.

episodes.label: Call Loan Market Seizure and Exchange Liquidity Crisis
episodes.summary: During the 1907 Panic, depositor runs on trust companies led to the seizure of the New York Stock Exchange call loan market, with overnight call loan rates spiking to 100% annualized and liquidity drying up; J.P. Morgan raised emergency funds to supply the NYSE to maintain trading operations.

episodes.label: NYCH Emergency Liquidity Measures and Deposit Convertibility Suspension
episodes.summary: During the Panic of 1907 on 1907-10-26, the New York Clearing House (NYCH) established a special loan issuance team to provide emergency liquidity support to its member banks via clearing house loan certificates, and coordinated all member banks to collectively suspend deposit convertibility into cash to mitigate widespread bank run pressures.

episodes.label: J.P. Morgan Led Private Sector Bailout Efforts
episodes.summary: During the 1907 Panic, J.P. Morgan coordinated private sector capital injections using personal funds and contributions from other New York bankers to support distressed trust companies, keep the New York Stock Exchange operational, and mitigate widespread liquidity shortages and bank runs.

episodes.label: Gold Imports and Liquidity Restoration
episodes.summary: Following the 1907 Panic deposit convertibility suspension by the New York Clearing House, a currency premium attracted gold imports from European financial centers to New York between November 1907 and January 1908, which ultimately restored liquidity to U.S. financial markets.

outcomes.label: The intervention efforts formed part of the liquidity-restoration phase of the panic.

stages.label: Trigger and Initial Member Bank Runs
stages.summary: 这次失败导致了与该计划有关的两家经纪公司的破产，并引发了与Heinze及Morse相关的银行及信托公司的挤兑; 4天后，纽清所发布公开告示称，经审查，与海因策有关的银行，如美国商业国家银行（Mercantile National Bank），仍有偿付能力

stages.label: Trust Company Runs and Systemic Crisis Onset
stages.summary: panic had spread to the trust companies between; depositor fear spread to the trust companies beginning on October 21 when they ran the Knickerbocker Trust

stages.label: Containment, Resolution and Systemic Reform Catalyst
stages.summary: 10月26日，经过不同寻常的5日延误，纽清所委员会召开会议，并成立了贷款投放特别小组; gold imports ultimately restored liquidity to financial markets
